capabilities: Export notes to Word, PDF, Markdown or LaTeX through pandoc
Turn wiki links into formatted citations with a reference list
Insert citations from a .bib bibliography at the cursor
Strip Obsidian-only content such as comments, tags and block IDs from exports
Apply custom Word templates and pandoc arguments
extras: Free, with donations via Liberapay. Requires Obsidian 1.13 or later on desktop. Includes an unusually detailed network and file disclosure and reproducible-release verification instructions; further documentation (architecture, FAQ) lives outside the README.
motivation: The author built it because a link that works in Obsidian means nothing when a chapter has to go to a supervisor as a Word file.
problem: Citation links that work inside Obsidian turn into dead text the moment a note has to leave the vault as a Word file or journal submission.

relations.evidence: It runs pandoc on your note to turn your links into real citations
export a .bib file from Zotero with Better BibTeX's auto-export turned on
when Better BibTeX changes a key, links made before still cite the paper
Works well with Paper Trail, which turns your Zotero library into a reading queue
In the Open publishes a note as a post on your own website
Take the Floor presents a note as slides, with your speaker notes on your own screen

requires.name: pandoc (or the built-in pandoc it offers to download)
TeX distribution with xelatex, for PDF export
Zotero with Better BibTeX auto-export, for citations

summary: Pandoc-based exporter that turns a note's links into real citations and exports it as Word, PDF, Markdown or LaTeX with a reference list.
